```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Growth to Standard
Considerations for defining a year’s worth of growth
Damian Betebenner
Center for Assessment

January 24th, 2023</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Catch-Up/Keep-Up</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Definitions
• Each student for whom growth is calculated (i.e., an SGP) is also
 has a growth target (i.e., SGP_TARGET) calculated.
 • If the student’s prior achievement is not proficient, then the
 SGP_TARGET is the growth target to catch-up to proficiency
 within 3 years or by the end of testing (time frame can be
 changed depending upon policy)
 • If the student’s prior achievement is proficient, then the
 SGP_TARGET is the growth target to keep-up to proficiency
 for the next 3 years or by the end of testing.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Definitions
• The SGP_TARGET:
 • Isn’t a guarantee that the student reaching the target will catch-up/
 keep-up.
 • It’s a one-year installment on a multi-year plan to catch-up/keep-up.
 • Requires an SGP in order to make a determination of catch-up/keep-up.
 • Will take on extremely high (above 90) or extremely low values (below
 10) for students who are low achievers and high achievers, respectively.
 • Can be converted to a RICAS scale score if desired.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/06.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Catch Up/Keep Up Drawback
• Though a technically correct approach, I believe using SGP
 and SGP_TARGET to communicate growth/learning goals
 suffers from the following problems:
 • Difficult to communicate and comprehend, especially for
 non-technical stakeholders
 • Difficulty in communication inhibits stakeholder use of the
 data
 • 1 to 99 scale communicates precision that isn’t justified.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/07.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">A Year’s Worth of Learning</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/08.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Year’s Worth of Learning
• Another approach that “coarsens” SGP and SGP_TARGET and
 utilizes the language of a “year’s worth of learning”.
• The terms “a year’s worth of learning” is often well received
 by non-technical stakeholders even though it is not well
 defined. We propose the following definitions:
 • At or near a year’s worth of learning: 30 ≤ SGP ≤ 65
 • Below a year’s worth of learning: SGP &lt; 30
 • Above a year’s worth of learning: SGP &gt; 65</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/09.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Year’s Worth of Learning
• Based upon these three categories of growth/learning, students
 are classified in two ways:
 • Category 1: Growth demonstrated in current year
 • Category 2: Growth needed/desired in current year
• Note, the two categories are analogous to SGP and SGP_TARGET
 except they are expressed in terms of the three “year’s worth of
 learning” levels instead of the 99 different percentiles.
• Note: Growth needed is to either catch up or keep up. That
 distinction is not made explicit.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/11.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Year’s Worth of Learning
• The qualifiers (not enough, enough, definitely not enough) are
 rough placeholders.
• The goal of systemic improvement is to diminish (over time) the
 percentage of students demonstrating less than a year’s worth of
 learning and to maximize (especially for the lowest achieving
 students) the percentage of students demonstrating more than a
 year’s worth of growth.
• Note: All of the calculations are done behind the scenes with SGP
 and SGP_TARGET, but the language used to communicate the
 results is “year’s worth of learning”.</div>
```
